description:
Canonical vectors for the callsign-blocklist gate, shared between MCProxy's MessageRouter.blocklist_decision (src/mcapp/main.py) and the webapp's mirror of it in processDataElement (src/services/messageProcessor.ts). Both sides classify an inbound payload from a blocked src as pass/redirect/drop using the same rules: strip the via-relay path off src before matching (first comma component), resolve dst to its effective target (last comma component of a via-routed 'VIA,TARGET'), and treat numeric groups plus '*'/'ALL'/'TEST' as group-like (redirect to the spam group) while everything else drops. `blocklist` entries are matched by EXACT string (no SSID normalization) against src, both sides upper-cased before comparison.

Each vector's `decision` is MCProxy's actual output (verified live against MessageRouter.blocklist_decision — see MCProxy/src/mcapp/send_path_tests.py). Where the webapp's mirror provably disagrees, the vector also carries `webapp_decision` plus a `note` explaining the divergence; both sides then assert their OWN real behavior against the correct field rather than papering over the mismatch. This file is vendored byte-for-byte (parsed-equal, not literal-byte-equal — Prettier reformats the webapp copy) at webapp/src/services/__tests__/blocklist_decision_vectors.json; a spec there diffs the two copies when both repos are checked out side by side.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE (documented, not fixed — code-simpl-v2.md item 4d): MCProxy's is_group() (src/mcapp/commands/parsing.py) enforces a 1..99999 numeric range for group dsts. The webapp's isGroupDst (src/utils/callsignUtils.ts) is a bare /^\d+$/ test with no range check. So an out-of-range numeric dst (e.g. '0', or 6+ digits like '100000') is classified group-like by the webapp but NOT by MCProxy — MCProxy drops such traffic from a blocked src while the webapp would redirect it to the spam group instead. Real MeshCom group ids never leave 1..99999 in practice, so this has no observed production impact; flagged here rather than patched because fixing either side is outside this vector-authoring task's remit.

vectors.name: blocked src + numeric group dst redirects to the spam group
blocked src + personal dst drops (not redirected)
blocked src + special group dst 'TEST' redirects
via-routed blocked src (sender is the first hop) + group dst redirects
via-routed blocked src + personal dst drops
via-routed group dst resolves from the LAST comma component
a blocked RELAY hop (not the sender) must NOT trigger the gate
SSID-specific block does not cover a different SSID of the same base call
base-callsign block does not cover any SSID'd variant (exact match only, no normalization)
lower-case incoming src is still matched (both sides upper-case before comparing)
numeric group dst at the upper boundary (99999) is still in-range on both sides
DIVERGENCE: dst '0' is out of MCProxy's 1..99999 group range but webapp's isGroupDst has no lower bound
vectors.note: MCProxy's is_group() requires 1 <= n <= 99999, so '0' is not a group and blocklist_decision drops. The webapp's isGroupDst (src/utils/callsignUtils.ts) is a bare /^\d+$/ test with no range check, so it treats '0' as group-like and redirects to the spam group instead. Not patched — see this file's top-level description.

vectors.name: DIVERGENCE: dst '100000' is out of MCProxy's 1..99999 group range but webapp's isGroupDst has no upper bound
vectors.note: Same divergence class as dst '0': MCProxy's is_group() caps at 99999, MCProxy drops. The webapp's isGroupDst has no upper bound, so it redirects. Not patched — see this file's top-level description.
